title: Moncton Home Rebates 2026: NB Power Heat Pump and Income Help
desc: Moncton home rebates for 2026: NB Power pays $1,500 for a central heat pump, $550 for a heat pump water heater, and the Enhanced program helps incomes under $70,000. Oil funding has closed.
lead: About half of Moncton households earned under $70,000 in 2020, which is the income line for NB Power's Enhanced Energy Savings Program. That makes Moncton a good place to check the income-based help before you pay for anything. Here is what is open on October 21, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open for Moncton homes in 2026
cards_intro: We read the NB Power pages on SaveEnergyNB on October 21, 2026. Each card shows the date and links to the source.

cards.title: Central ducted heat pump
cards.note: On NB Power's qualifying list. $400 for a mini split, $2,000 geothermal, $350 per head multizone.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: ENERGY STAR. Drain water heat recovery pays $400.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: By R-value added. Insulate at least 20% of an area.

cards.title: Windows, HRV, air sealing
cards.note: Windows, doors and skylights $50 each, HRV $200, air sealing by leakage drop.

cards.title: Income under $70,000
cards.note: Combined household income under $70,000. First come, first served while funding lasts.

cards.title: Oil to heat pump advance
cards.note: Registration closed June 30, 2026. Finish by March 31, 2027 if you registered.

sections:
The 2021 Census counted 35,120 households in the City of Moncton. Four numbers matter for rebates:

  • Income. The median household total income was $68,000 in 2020. About 52% of households earned under $70,000, and about 19% earned under $35,000. These are before-tax Census figures, not the Enhanced program's own test.
  • Owners and renters. 56% own and 44% rent.
  • Older homes. About 46% were built before 1981.
  • Kinds of homes. 14,770 houses are single-detached (42%), 4,380 are semi-detached, and 10,595 are apartments in buildings under five storeys.

2,025 homes (6%) needed major repairs. Repairs come first, because insulation does little in a home with a leaky roof.

The Enhanced Energy Savings Program is for homeowners with a combined household income under $70,000. NB Power checks line 15000 of each adult's latest Notice of Assessment, and you must own and live in the home. If your home has electric baseboards and no mini split, NB Power may recommend one. If you heat only with an oil furnace or boiler, it may recommend a cold climate heat pump. Places are first come, first served while funding lasts, so register early. If you are already in Total Home, email SmartHabits@nbpower.com. Given the Census income numbers, many Moncton households are close enough to the line to be worth a check.
The Total Home steps in Moncton

The usual path is the Total Home Energy Savings Program. You register online or call 1-800-663-6272. A Certified Energy Advisor does your Home Energy Evaluation. You pick upgrades from the report and have 9 months to finish them. The advisor then checks the work and gives you a new EnerGuide rating, and you get your rebates from your receipts, by e-Transfer or direct deposit. Book the evaluation before you buy anything, because the evaluation unlocks the rebates.
Heat pumps and water heaters in Moncton

A central ducted air source heat pump earns $1,500, a mini split $400, a furnace add-on $1,000 and a geothermal system $2,000. A multizone system pays $350 for each indoor head. The unit must be on NB Power's qualifying list. A heat pump water heater earns $550. The oil to heat pump advance payment closed to new registrations on June 30, 2026. Ottawa's National Heat Pump Rebate is expected in early 2027, and how it combines with NB Power is not published. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.
claim_steps: Check whether your combined household income is under $70,000. If yes, register for the Enhanced Energy Savings Program.
Otherwise, register for Total Home online or call 1-800-663-6272.
Get the Home Energy Evaluation before you buy anything.
Finish the upgrades within 9 months and keep every receipt.
Get the final inspection, then your rebates.
faq: How much is the heat pump rebate in Moncton?

$1,500 for a central ducted air source heat pump, $1,000 for a furnace add-on, $2,000 for geothermal, $400 for a mini split and $350 per indoor head for multizone. The unit must be on NB Power's list.
Is there income-based help in Moncton?
Yes. The Enhanced Energy Savings Program is for homeowners with a combined household income under $70,000, first come, first served while funding lasts.
Is the oil to heat pump funding still open in Moncton?
No. Registration for the advance payment closed on June 30, 2026. People who registered must finish by March 31, 2027.
Do I need an energy evaluation first?
Yes. The Total Home Energy Savings Program starts with a Home Energy Evaluation by a Certified Energy Advisor. Book it before you buy upgrades.
Does Moncton have its own home energy rebate?
We found no City of Moncton home energy rebate on NB Power's pages. The money comes from NB Power's programs.
